title: How Finch Legal Uses Reducto to Help Paralegals Manage 5x More Personal Injury Cases
summary: See how Finch Legal uses Reducto to turn every inbound document into structured, cited data, helping its paralegals manage 5x more personal injury cases.
body_markdown:
> *“Every document that enters Finch runs through Reducto. It gives our paralegals a clear, cited view of the information that matters, so they can quickly understand what changed and take action.”*


> *— Faris Ibrahim, Member of Technical Staff at Finch Legal*


### Building an operating system for personal injury cases


Personal injury cases generate a sprawling trail of information.


A case may begin with a signed retainer and HIPAA authorization, then accumulate medical records, police reports, witness statements, insurance coverage information, driver’s licenses, letters of representation, and other correspondence. Some documents arrive from hospitals or insurance companies, while others are collected through accounts online or exchanged over email.


Finch Legal helps personal injury firms manage this pre-litigation work. Founded in 2024, the company operates as a services-first business: clients work with Finch Legal’s paralegals, while the technology helping those paralegals work remains behind the scenes.


The platform includes AI agents that run around the clock, providing in-house paralegals tools to handle substantially larger caseloads. Faris Ibrahim, a member of Finch Legal’s technical staff, estimates that its paralegals can manage five to ten times the caseload of a typical paralegal at another firm. The operating model creates a tight feedback loop between Finch Legal’s engineers and the people doing the legal work. Because the paralegals are in-house, engineers can observe where workflows slow down, release a change, and learn from its use almost immediately.


> “Because our paralegals are in-house, our engineers see their workflows firsthand. We can ship something, watch them use it, and start iterating within 30 minutes.” — Faris Ibrahim, Member of Technical Staff at Finch Legal


### The bottleneck is reconstruction


When Faris joined Finch, the largest opportunity he found was the cost a paralegal pays every time they pick a case back up after time away from it. Before they can update a client, they have to rebuild the picture from scratch: what information is already on hand, what the parties have said to each other since, and whether the status of the case has moved. That preparation can take 30 minutes before a single phone call, and it happens again the next time the file resurfaces. Finch Legal’s goal is to have the current state of the case waiting for the paralegal instead.


That picture is spread thin across a large document set. An average Finch Legal case carries roughly 250 documents, and Faris estimated that around 90% of the firm’s cases involve motor vehicles, so the same categories of paperwork recur from file to file in slightly different formats. Reading any one of those records is trivial, since a paralegal can open it and understand it in seconds. The cost sits in the volume and the sequence, because what a single record means depends on everything already in the file and on what has been done with it since.


Finch Legal treats that as an engineering problem rather than a staffing one. If the state of a case can be assembled as the documents arrive, the half hour of catch-up drops out of every client conversation, and what is left for the paralegal is the judgment work they were hired for. Getting there depends on the documents themselves being readable by software.


### Making every document machine-readable with Reducto


Reducto has been part of Finch Legal’s architecture from the beginning, sitting at the point where every inbound document first enters the system.


The team knew it needed reliable OCR and document parsing, but traceability was equally important. In legal work, extracted information is most useful when a paralegal can quickly return to its original location in the source document.


Reducto provides Finch Legal with structured text, page-level information, section headings, and the location data needed to create citations. Finch Legal normalizes that output into its internal formats while retaining the associated Reducto JSON. That normalized document layer then supports Finch Legal’s downstream systems. Depending on the document, the platform can classify it, update relevant case information, identify signatures or forms, generate citations, or initiate another workflow.


> “Reducto is the foundation of our document workflows. Every document goes through it before we classify the information, update the case, generate citations, or decide what needs someone’s attention.” — Faris Ibrahim, Member of Technical Staff at Finch Legal


A document that arrives at Finch Legal is not merely stored and indexed for later retrieval. It becomes an event, something that can change the state of a case the moment it lands.


That evaluation happens as the document lands. Faris built a tool that assesses new information as it arrives, whether it reaches the firm as a document, an email, or a text message from a client, working out how it affects the case and whether it introduces risk that should reach a paralegal immediately. One document may require a signature, another may need to be routed to a particular person, and another may update the case quietly without anyone’s attention.


That triage matters when every paralegal is carrying a large caseload. Instead of monitoring every file for every change, the team can spend its attention on the developments that call for judgment. Document ingestion, in other words, is the beginning of Finch Legal’s operational workflows, not a separate administrative step.


### Citations give paralegals a path back to the evidence


When asked which feature paralegals value most, Faris’s answer was immediately citations.


Finch Legal’s paralegals, and the firms they partner with, can see information extracted from their documents and navigate back to the relevant source location. Reducto’s citation information helps Finch Legal expose that connection within an interface designed around legal workflows.


That traceability helps Finch Legal combine automation with human review. Its systems can organize information, surface changes, and initiate workflows, while the people handling the case retain access to the underlying documents.


### What’s next


Finch Legal started narrow. Its paralegals worked as an extension of established firms, learning each firm’s habits while running on the company’s own platform underneath. Now, after spending two years inside other firms’ processes, they are building out their own legal team to run cases end to end.


Documents stay at the center of that and Reducto turns them into structured, traceable text, which is what the rest of Finch Legal’s automation is built on. The paperwork will keep arriving, in greater volume as Finch Legal takes on more of the lifecycle itself, and we are glad to be the layer sitting underneath it.
